correctness.rationale: The normalization A^T A=A1^T(I+Y^T Y)A1 and positive definiteness reduce the spectrum to a Rayleigh ratio. The completed-square identity and ||Yv||/||v|| differing from ||Wv||/||v|| by at most epsilon prove both spectral bounds. A diagonal 2x2 witness attains both endpoints simultaneously. SPD similarity yields the G-energy Richardson factor and balancing the endpoints gives tau*=2/(2+epsilon^2). For residual consistency, choose r2=u and r1=-Y^T u; then A^T r=0 but the W correction is nonzero whenever W!=Y. The scalar inconsistent example has z(e)h(e)<0, so the quadratic objective strictly increases for every tau>0. Numerical tests are corroborative only.
residual_risks: Assumes exact arithmetic, exact upper-block solve, fixed W and an absolute operator-norm error bound; does not prove convergence of every ILU, flexible Krylov or floating-point implementation.

value.rationale: Row splitting creates a concrete design choice: using an approximate factor with the true normal residual has a dimension-independent sharp spectral guarantee, while inserting the same inaccurate factor inside the residual can destroy least-squares stationarity and produce ascent even for arbitrarily small error. The simultaneous extremizer and exact minimax step make the error bound operational rather than merely sufficient.
residual_risks: The practical benefit of evaluating the true normal residual, memory cost, finite precision and iterative-solver runtime are not quantified.
